newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of atrocities.
newsitem.headline: Sudan accuses Ethiopia of atrocities.

text.p: An official Sudanese report accused Ethiopia on Wednesday of looting, rape and killings in two towns Sudan says were seized last month by Ethiopian and Khartoum opposition forces.

Ethiopia has denied charges by Sudan's Islamist government it is behind rebel attacks led by the Sudan People's Liberation Army, which gained momentum last month with the fall of Kirmuk and Qissan along its border with Sudan.
Khartoum's accusations about what happened when the towns fell into rebel hands could not be independently confirmed.

"Extra-judicial killings, beating, torture, rape and other forms of brutal practises were among the atrocities committed by the Ethiopian Tigrayan Forces and so-called alliance forces against civilians in the Sudanese border towns of Kirmuk and Qissan when they invaded them on January 12," the report said.

"The invasion of Kirmuk and Qissan towns was carried out by 3,000 heavily armed Ethiopian infantry troops after heavy Ethiopian artillery and tank shelling from inside the Ethiopian territories," said the report, carried by the official Sudan news agency SUNA.
It said some 5,000 civilians who fled were rounded up and some were "randomly picked out and executed before others. Three women were raped..." It said some 600 people were killed.
An alliance of northern and southern rebels, bent on toppling the government of Khartoum, launched the offensive across Sudan's eastern and southern borders.
